title: The Global Evolution of Remote Work Policies
subtitle: An examination of how the post-pandemic workplace is shifting from emergency flexibility to structured hybrid models.
description: This series tracks the transition from the 2020 remote work surge to current return-to-office mandates. It explores the economic, social, and managerial tensions defining the future of global labor.

articles.label: Part 1
articles.note: The initial rapid adoption of remote work during the pandemic and the immediate organizational challenges faced by global firms.

articles.label: Part 2
articles.note: The conflicting priorities between leadership seeking office presence and employees valuing flexibility.

articles.label: Part 3
articles.note: The shift from voluntary remote work to formal return-to-office (RTO) mandates and the resulting friction.

articles.label: Part 4
articles.note: The broader effects of remote work on city centers, local economies, and individual well-being.

articles.label: Part 5
articles.note: The long-term outlook for labor laws, technology, and the definition of 'work' in a globalized economy.
